subject.title: fix(sessions): sweep orphan store temp files

question: Should OpenClaw delete stale matching session-store temp files during ordinary session-store load/cache miss, or keep deletion limited to explicit cleanup and disk-budget flows?
rationale: The patch is technically focused, but it changes the production session-load boundary from read-only/cache work into a filesystem deletion point, which is a session-state merge-risk decision maintainers should explicitly own.

options.title: Accept Load-Time Sweep
options.body: Proceed after conflict resolution, treating stale matching temp deletion during load as the intended fix for the linked disk-leak report.

options.title: Share Cleanup Rule First
options.body: Ask for a small refactor that reuses the existing stale-temp cutoff helper before landing, reducing drift between load-time and disk-budget cleanup.

options.title: Limit Cleanup To Explicit Flows
options.body: Pause or close this branch if maintainers want temp deletion to remain only in doctor, cleanup-service, or disk-budget paths.

recommendation.title: Accept Load-Time Sweep
recommendation.body: Proceed after conflict resolution, treating stale matching temp deletion during load as the intended fix for the linked disk-leak report.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete merged the prior session temp cleanup work and is the strongest available owner signal for accepting this session-state boundary.
